analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. It touches docs/developer/build.md, navigation.md and test.md, and removes the retained-console build/test/hosting instructions (the `make ui-*` targets, the `lint-console` CI lane row, and the Retained Console sections). It also reassigns ownership of the shared wire fixtures (paged_footprint_wire.json, process_memory_wire.json) to the platform repository.

No executable code, workflow YAML, protocol handling, key custody, attestation, cache or fan-helper paths are changed in the supplied units. The threat-model assets and boundaries are therefore untouched at runtime: TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011, TB-012, T-041 and the App Attest and add-on-hold entries.

Things I checked:
- The build.md runner routing table and the App Attest, Dev Build Identity and release-qualification text still describe the existing controls. The routing text still says release, signing, publication, model registration and cache-swift keep literal Blacksmith labels, so no new trust in the sandbox plane for signing lanes is introduced.
- navigation.md now says console code lives in the platform repo and drops the console snapshot rows. This is an ownership clarification, not a control change.
- test.md now states that the platform keeps byte-identical fixture copies. The only residual risk is documentation or process drift if the provider and platform fixtures diverge. That is not a security regression.

Remaining questions for integration:
- The patch excerpts are truncated, and the build.md base text and several deletions are not fully visible. The actual removal of console-ui, Makefile targets, CI jobs and fixtures is outside these units, so I cannot confirm that the other files in the PR stay consistent with these docs.
- Whether the removed `lint-console` job or console tests had security-relevant gating is not evidenced here.
